🎯 Key Takeaways for quick navigation:

00:00 🧪 Introduction to AI Model Testing
- Introduction and purpose of testing AI models, specifically GPT-4, Gemini Pro, and Grok.
- Discussion about the public skepticism towards Google Gemini's results.
- Aim to test various capabilities like reasoning, writing, creativity, coding, and vision.
01:21 🍎 Vision Test with Apples
- Testing AI models' ability to count apples in images.
- Both models struggle with accurate counting.
- Additional tests with different images to challenge the models.
02:18 🧮 Geometry Problem Solving
- Models are tasked with solving geometry problems using images.
- GPT-4's performance compared with Gemini in solving mathematical questions based on images.
- Gemini's inaccuracies in providing correct answers.
03:11 🚗 Speedometer and Odometer Analysis
- Analyzing images of speedometers and odometers to determine speeds and distances.
- Gemini's and GPT-4's varied success in interpreting and reasoning with these images.
- Specific instances where models correctly or incorrectly estimate values.
04:12 🗼 Landmark Recognition Test
- AI models are tested on their ability to recognize famous landmarks from images.
- Comparison of Gemini's and GPT-4's accuracy in identifying landmarks.
- Detailed analysis of each model's response to different landmarks.
05:20 🍲 Food Identification Challenge
- Testing models' ability to identify dishes from images.
- Gemini's and GPT-4's responses to various food images, highlighting their strengths and weaknesses.
- Special focus on a dish with limited visual clues.
06:15 🖼️ Hidden Message in Image Test
- Exploring models' capabilities in deciphering hidden messages in images.
- Detailed steps of how Gemini and GPT-4 approach and solve (or fail to solve) the challenge.
- Analysis of models' strategies in interpreting binary codes in images.
08:33 🃏 Humor Understanding with Jokes
- Evaluating how well AI models understand and explain jokes.
- Comparison of Gemini's and GPT-4's abilities to interpret humor in various joke formats.
- Specific examples demonstrating the models' comprehension of humor.
10:11 🏝️ Cultural Reference and Joke Analysis
- Testing models on cultural references and humor understanding using a cartoon character.
- Detailed analysis of models' responses to a joke involving the character Maui.
- Gemini and GPT-4's varied abilities to connect cultural references with humor.
13:19 🎼 Music Generation Task
- AI models are challenged to create music using ABC notation.
- Evaluation of Gemini's and GPT-4's musical compositions based on a specific prompt.
- Comparison of the models' ability to adhere to the prompt's requirements.
14:42 🎭 Plato Dialogue Creation Task
- Models are asked to write a dialogue by Plato criticizing autoregressive language models.
- Analysis of each model's approach to the task, focusing on style and philosophical depth.
- Detailed comparison of the dialogues created by Gemini and GPT-4.
19:27 🎨 Kandinsky Style Art Generation Challenge
- Tasking AI models to generate JavaScript code for creating random images in Kandinsky's style.
- Evaluation of the models' success in understanding and implementing the art style.
- Comparison of the visual outputs produced by each model.
20:24 🐔 Browser Game Development Challenge
- Challenge for models to create a simple browser game involving chickens.
- Analysis of each model's approach and the functionality of the games they develop.
- Specific details on the models' performance in game development.
22:53 🔍 Mystery Solving Task
- Models are given clues to solve a fictional murder mystery.
- Detailed examination of how each model processes information and arrives at a conclusion.
- Comparison of Gemini's and GPT-4's logical reasoning abilities.
24:16 📊 Final Tally and Overall Assessment
- Summary of the models' performance across all tasks.
- Comprehensive evaluation of Gemini's and GPT-4's strengths and weaknesses in various areas.
- Final scores and reflections on each model's capabilities.

Made with HARPA AI

comments.author: @DeliciousHoneyDewDew2
comments.text:
I'm not sure why more YouTube reviewers haven't tested out Gemini like you did. I evaluated it the same night, not to critique it but because I needed it for my business. While Gemini performed better than prior Bard demos, overall it was quite subpar for my professional purposes. Claude still seems the most capable of the three to me.

I do have major issues with the censorship Claude enforces, so I'm constantly working around its limits. This all leads me to three conclusions: first, much of the AI hype exceeds current realities. Yes, attaining advanced AGI and ASI could enable transformative change but we seem far from that still. Second, we may be nearing the limits of the transformer-based model. And third, the fastest way for Google to strengthen Gemini is to release it publicly now and learn from wider user testing. Doing so would have prevented this embarrassing week.

comments.author: @ReflectionOcean
comments.text:
GPT-4 excels in vision tasks, completing 85% of the tasks compared to Gemini's 11%.
GPT-4 also performs well in writing and reasoning tasks, scoring 39 points out of a possible 47.
Grok does not perform as well as GPT-4 in vision tasks, but it does well in writing and reasoning tasks, scoring 32 points.
Grok also excels in real-time data tasks, which were not tested in this video.
Bard performs the worst overall, scoring only 19 points.
Bard does well in some humor tasks, but it struggles with vision, coding, and reasoning tasks.

comments.text:
The first time through, I didn't look carefully at the Aunt Agatha puzzle. But the second time, I have questions. 

Let's let A = Agatha, B = Butler, C = Charles and A_h = set of people A hates, B_h = set of people B hates; C_h = set of people C hates.

By (5), A hates everyone except the B. A_h = {A, C}
By (7), B also hates {A, C}. (B cannot hate himself since by (8) no one hates everyone.)
So A_h = B_h = {A, C}

By (4), C hates either {} of {B}. So C is not the killer since A not in C_h.

When eliminating suspects, ChatGPT says that A not in B_h, so B is not the killer. (But that contradicts what we already know, i.e., B_h = {A, C}.)

ChatGPT then concludes that A is the killer. But that is based on faulty logic.

To continue solving the puzzle, 
We already know that B_h does not include B. But by (6) B_h consists of all people not richer than A. So B must be richer than A.
Since B is richer than A, by (3) B did not kill A.

Having ruled out B and C as the killer, the only possibility left is that A is the killer.

As far as I can tell ChatGPT didn't make use of (6) in its solution. So it got the right answer, but it did so through faulty logic.
